flashcard_questions.q: Which 1794 collection contains Blake’s poem London?
Which repeated word suggests London is owned and controlled?
What does Blake mean by ‘mind-forg’d manacles’?
flashcard_questions.a: People are trapped psychologically by the systems of those in power.

flashcard_questions.q: Which institution does Blake call ‘black’ning’ for failing the poor?
Whose blood runs down the Palace walls in Blake’s third stanza?
Which oxymoron ends the poem London?
Which rhyme scheme runs through the four quatrains of London?
Which country did John Agard grow up in?
What does a Eurocentric education mean?
flashcard_questions.a: Teaching centred on European culture and history at the expense of others.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Haitian revolutionary does Agard call ‘de beacon’?
Which Crimean War nurse is ‘a healing star among the wounded’?
How does Agard separate the two histories visually on the page?
flashcard_questions.a: Black history stanzas are printed in italics, European ones in standard text.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Agard’s phonetic spelling of ‘Dem’ assert?
flashcard_questions.a: His Caribbean identity, resisting the dominance of Standard English.

flashcard_questions.q: Which violent metaphor shows his education hid his own culture?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Bandage up me eye with me own history.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which verb shows that reclaiming identity is hard physical work?

notes: 15 cards across both poems, 7 on London and 8 on Checking Out Me History: 6 quotation-recall fronts, 3 quotation-to-effect (‘mind-forg’d manacles’, the ‘Dem’ spelling, ‘carving’), 2 structure-and-form (the ABAB quatrains, the italic dual structure), 2 figure identification (Toussaint, Mary Seacole), 2 context cards (Songs of Experience, Guyana and Eurocentric schooling). ‘Industrial Revolution’, ‘manacles’ and ‘oxymoron’ dropped as glossary restatements already tested by the quotation cards; Nanny de Maroon trimmed to keep the three figure cards from interfering. All quotations verbatim from the lesson content.
